_comment: MCP server config loaded by the `claude` CLI in agent/Dockerfile's image (see docker-compose.yml `agent` service, --mcp-config). Plain JSON has no comment syntax, so notes live in these _comment keys instead — the `claude` CLI ignores unknown keys, and the sibling Jobs project's docker/mcp.json (heavily-commented everywhere else) is itself comment-free, evidence the same convention already held there. ${VAR:-default} below is Claude Code's documented env-var expansion for .mcp.json; it reads this container's actual environment (docker-compose.yml `agent` service), so it stays correct if either default ever changes there.
_browserDriverComment: TWO browser drivers are declared below and BOTH are real. Which one the agent may actually use on a given run is decided by AGENT_BROWSER_DRIVER (docker-compose.yml `agent` service, default `browser`), which agent/daily-apply.sh reads to build the `claude --allowedTools` list: only the selected driver's tools are granted. Declaring both here is harmless — an MCP server the agent holds no tool grant for is never called — and it keeps the switch a one-variable change rather than a config rewrite. Do not grant both at once: two ways to drive a browser, with no rule saying which, is how an unattended run ends up applying from the wrong session.

truthcv._comment: TruthCV's own tool surface: generate_cover_letter, record_application, record_screening, check_cooldown, get_canonical_cv, get_profile_answers, record_company_board, get_job_profiles, recommend_salary. REST routes at GET /mcp/tools and POST /mcp/tools/{name} (agenttools/server.py) provide HTTP access; JSON-RPC streamable-HTTP endpoint at POST /mcp (agenttools/mcp_app.py, registered via Server.streamable_http_app() with json_response=True, stateless_http=True) is what this `http` type MCP server calls. The default is the in-network address of the `app` compose service — reachable only from inside the compose network, not from the host or the open internet.

browser._comment: DEFAULT browser driver (AGENT_BROWSER_DRIVER=browser). @playwright/mcp serving headful Chromium under Xvfb in the `browser` compose service (browser/Dockerfile, browser/entrypoint.sh). Exposes browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_file_upload, browser_snapshot, browser_take_screenshot and the rest of the upstream Playwright MCP tool set, which is why agent/daily-apply.sh grants the whole server as `mcp__browser` rather than enumerating tools. The default is the in-network address of the `browser` service — reachable only from inside the compose network, not from the host or the open internet. The container keeps a persistent Chromium profile on a named volume, so a one-time manual login through the noVNC viewport at http://localhost:7900 survives restarts, and it mounts the app data volume read-only at /app/data so browser_file_upload can resolve the `path` get_canonical_cv returns.

interceptor._comment: OPT-IN browser driver (AGENT_BROWSER_DRIVER=interceptor), for a host that actually runs Interceptor. The `claude` CLI spawns `interceptor mcp serve` over stdio in-container; that subprocess shells to the real `interceptor <verb>` command, which dials the bind-mounted unix socket at INTERCEPTOR_SOCKET_PATH to reach the HOST interceptor daemon, which in turn reaches Chrome via native messaging. Its draw over the containerised `browser` service is that it inherits the operator's existing logged-in ATS/SSO sessions instead of needing them established once through noVNC. It requires the host binary bind-mounted at INTERCEPTOR_BIN and a live daemon on the socket — agent/entrypoint.sh and agent/daily-apply.sh check both, but ONLY when this driver is selected, and agent/smoke-test.sh proves the whole chain including that the Bun-compiled binary actually loads under this image's glibc.

_fallbackComment: HISTORY, so neither design is reinstated or discarded by mistake. The ORIGINAL plan was to drive the operator's real, already-logged-in HOST Chrome through an `interceptor` daemon over a bind-mounted unix socket, with a containerised Playwright browser as the documented fallback. That was retired because the primary path appeared to be software that did not exist: neither this repo nor the retiring Jobs repo contained an interceptor MCP server or its launch command; Jobs merely allow-listed mcp__interceptor__interceptor_{browser,read,local} against a server declared in the operator's personal Claude config, plus a Chrome extension its own docs record as NOT INSTALLED as of 2026-08-12. The containerised browser above replaced it: a real, running MCP server, sessions on a persistent profile volume, in its own container so a browser crash cannot take the agent loop down, with logins established once through the noVNC viewport. That replacement stands and is the DEFAULT. What has since changed is the premise, not the verdict: Interceptor does ship a real `interceptor mcp serve` stdio MCP server, and the operator's host runs it (a Bun-compiled binary and a live daemon on /tmp/interceptor.sock, both verified). So the interceptor entry above is no longer a phantom and is kept as a selectable driver for hosts that have it — but it is opt-in, because it depends on host state this repo does not control and cannot test in CI, whereas the `browser` service is self-contained. Choose with AGENT_BROWSER_DRIVER; do not delete either entry without reading both of these paragraphs.
